prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1441; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle contacted the claimant's vehicle on the driver side rear quarter panel. Claimant reports neck strain and stiffness since the impact and states she was seen at an urgent care facility the same day. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Recorded statement scheduled.

Entry 2: Recorded statement obtained from the claimant. She states the other vehicle drifted into her lane without signaling as she was passing. Insured driver's account differs slightly, stating the claimant was in the blind spot and accelerating. Both accounts logged. Scene photos requested from both parties and received from claimant. Police report requested and pending.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report. Responding officer noted both vehicles had damage consistent with a sideswipe and cited no one at scene. Witness listed on report not yet reached. Left voicemail. Reviewed claimant's photos, which show scrape marks on the rear door and bumper. Insured vehicle damage matches the described contact point.

Entry 4: Claimant provided urgent care records and a referral to a physical therapist. Records document neck strain diagnosis with a recommended course of physical therapy and over-the-counter pain management. Claimant advised of her right to seek medical treatment of her choosing and to request an itemized bill for all treatment. Claimant indicated she is still working with reduced hours and will provide wage documentation.

Entry 5: Witness reached by phone and confirmed the insured vehicle changed lanes without checking its mirrors, though witness could not say whether the claimant was in the blind spot. Liability appears to lean toward the insured driver. Claimant's physical therapy authorization reviewed and approved for an initial evaluation. File referred to supervisor for liability determination and reserve review. Follow-up with claimant scheduled after therapy progress report.
